title: Login and MFA endpoints: inspect, bypass or exempt from authentication

prose.text: For identity and MFA endpoints (see [[zia.saas-apps]] for the other causes) the question is whether the traffic must be decrypted (a control needs to read or edit it) or must not be (the client refuses the certificate).

prose.label: Must be inspected.
prose.text: Microsoft login hosts need decryption for tenant restriction, and the SSL rule that selects them has to win the order: [[zia.saas-apps.tenant-restriction-order]]; the hosts and headers are in [[zia.tenant-profiles.wire-mechanic]]. Webex Login Services follows the same prerequisite in [[zia.tenant-profiles.ssl-prerequisite]].

prose.label: Must not be inspected.
prose.text: A client that pins its own CA bundle cannot be inspected: [[zia.ssl-inspection.uninspectable]]. Which Duo hostnames to bypass is open {{gap:duo-endpoints}}. How narrowly to write any such bypass is in [[zia.ssl-inspection.exemptions]]. The predefined Click-to-Run exemption uses the stronger Bypass Other Policies setting ([[zia.ssl-inspection.exemptions]], `predefined-exemptions-differ`); whether it is the only predefined rule that does is gap `only-bypass-other-policies-rule`.

prose.label: Authentication exemptions are a different list.
prose.text: {{auth-exemption-not-ssl-bypass}} Enabling the Microsoft-Recommended One Click option adds one for Microsoft: {{one-click-auth-exemption}} The product-wide 25,000-entry pool the exemption URLs draw on is described in [[zia.authentication.exemptions]]; it is shared with custom URL categories and other lists, so it is not an independent 25,000-entry list as the old catalog implied. Typical entries are open {{gap:auth-exempt-login-hosts}}.

one-click-auth-exemption.statement: Enabling the Microsoft-Recommended One Click configuration also makes the Zscaler service configure an authentication exemption for Microsoft domains automatically.

quotes: The Zscaler service automatically configures authentication exemption for Microsoft domains.

auth-exemption-not-ssl-bypass.statement: The authentication exemption list and an SSL Inspection bypass are separate configuration objects with separate effects: an exemption skips the authentication challenge for a destination, while a Do Not Inspect rule skips decryption; exempting a host from one does not exempt it from the other.
auth-exemption-not-ssl-bypass.conditions: Inferred from the two being different objects (the auth exemption list and SSL rules). No source compares them.

duo-endpoints.title: Duo endpoints that need an SSL bypass
duo-endpoints.detail: Unverified legacy statement: bypass `*.duosecurity.com` and `*.duo.com`, plus `*.azureauth.duosecurity.com` for the Entra External MFA flow, because CA-bundle pinning means inspection breaks the TLS channel before any authentication happens. The legacy cited Duo's own documentation (duo.com/docs/duo-desktop, Duo KB 9585), which is not a registered source; the Zscaler guides do not mention Duo. See also zia.ssl-inspection.uninspectable:ca-bundle-pinned-vendor-apps for the pinning claim.
duo-endpoints.blocks: listing the hostnames to exempt for Duo

only-bypass-other-policies-rule.title: Whether Click-to-Run is the only predefined rule that uses Bypass Other Policies
only-bypass-other-policies-rule.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Microsoft 365 Click-to-Run - Zscaler's own predefined SSL rule uses Do Not Inspect + Bypass Other Policies. The only predefined rule using that more-dangerous variant." The guide's example table shows Click-to-Run as Bypass Other Policies and the Zscaler Recommended Exemptions rule as Evaluate Other Policies (zia.ssl-inspection.exemptions:predefined-exemptions-differ). The UCaaS One Click and IoT predefined rules are not shown with their setting there, so "only" is not supported.

auth-exempt-login-hosts.title: Common authentication-exemption entries
auth-exempt-login-hosts.detail: Unverified legacy statement: common Authentication Exemptions entries are `login.windows.net`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, OS update endpoints and captive-portal probes. The One Click option adds Microsoft domain exemptions on its own, but no source lists these entries as typical. The wider question is zia.authentication.exemptions:typical-entries.
